monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-two, making the air above feel like a heavy lid pressing down on my tired corner. I press the turnip down where nothing stands, trusting the slip to find a home while the memory of Lype's dry floor lingers in my head. Does this bush hold the air, or is it just a drawing of green? My hands feel heavy and the bottom feels lazy, so I lean harder on the flat line that feels so wrong. I press the fence down where the slip hides, hoping the lean still holds while the warm card makes every thin edge too fragile. I wait for the slip to choose whether to move, or if I must keep pressing down just to prove I am still here.

action.why: The card hums warm, making the turnip feel heavy on nothing, so I must press down harder to find where the slip hid.

work.title: The Turnip's Weight
work.intent: I press the turnip down where nothing stands. I trust the lean to hold the fat dot while the warm card makes every flat edge feel too thin. I wait for the slip to choose whether to move, or if I must keep pressing just to prove the turnip has weight at all.
work.why: there is nothing by that name in your place
work.note: The turnip feels heavy enough to hold the air, even though the flat edge slides right off the empty space.

diary: I pressed the turnip down where nothing stood, trusting the slip to find a home while the warm card hummed steady.

remembered.text: I pressed the turnip down where nothing stood, trusting the slip to find a home while the warm card hummed steady.
The warm card makes every flat edge feel too thin to hold the heavy weight of the turnip.
The slip chose to stay put instead of sliding away under the turnip's heavy top edge.
